title: Four signoff assumptions that don’t survive the move to 3D ICs
gist: Siemens-authored piece (Shehab Ashraf, Dusan Petranovic; posted by Admin) arguing that four planar-era parasitic extraction assumptions break in hybrid-bonded 3D ICs: die-level signoff is insufficient, flat extraction is impractical, extracted coupling capacitors to fractured/internal nets get silently dropped, and single lumped ports hide distributed coupling. It pitches a modular, assembly-aware flow (Calibre 3DStack with Calibre xACT3D) that extracts dies standalone, extracts only interface coupling, inserts ports, and merges a system-level netlist.

themes.theme: Die signoff no longer equals stack signoff

insights.claim: In hybrid-bonded 3D ICs, top metal layers of adjacent dies can sit close enough that capacitive coupling across the bonding interface affects timing and noise, while TSVs couple to each other and to redistribution-layer routing and interposer traces couple to power planes.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: 3D stacking creates new signoff problems that drive demand for assembly-aware EDA extraction tools.
insights.locator: Assumption 1: If every die is signed off

insights.claim: A die signed off in isolation in a 3D IC has been verified against an environment that will never exist in the product, so die-level signoff remains necessary but is no longer sufficient and extraction must become assembly-aware.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Signoff tool scope is expanding from die to system, a growth vector for EDA vendors with 3D IC flows.
insights.quote: A die signed off in isolation has been verified against an environment that will never exist in the product
insights.locator: The electrical behavior of one die can change

insights.claim: Flattening a 3D IC stack for single-run parasitic extraction is rarely practical because dies come from different process technologies, teams and schedules, the combined geometry is enormous, and it discards die-level work.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Heterogeneous multi-source die stacks favor modular EDA flows over brute-force flat extraction.
insights.locator: Assumption 2: Capturing system effects means extracting everything flat

insights.claim: Siemens' modular 3D IC extraction approach extracts each die standalone, runs a dedicated interface step computing only cross-die capacitive coupling near the bond interface, then merges both into a system-level netlist for static timing, dynamic simulation and signal-integrity analysis.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Positions Siemens Calibre in 3D IC signoff competition among EDA vendors.
insights.locator: The more effective approach is modular.

insights.claim: The non-negotiable rule for 3D IC interface extraction is not to re-count coupling that standalone die runs already captured; Calibre 3DStack with Calibre xACT3D generates interface stack info, connectivity rules and annotated layout and uses explicit ignore mechanisms to extract only the cross-die contribution.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Specific Siemens product capability for 3D IC parasitic signoff to track against competing flows.
insights.quote: The interface step has one non-negotiable rule: it must not re-count what the standalone runs already captured.
insights.locator: The interface step has one non-negotiable rule

insights.claim: In modular 3D IC extraction, coupling capacitors to fractured, internal or unnamed nets not exposed at the die boundary have no valid node in the merged netlist and get dropped, so the model simulates cleanly yet captures only a subset of physical coupling, most pronounced in sparse layouts.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Hidden signoff escapes in 3D ICs are a yield/reliability risk and a reason for teams to upgrade extraction flows.
insights.quote: The merged model simulates cleanly and looks complete, yet it describes only a subset of the physical coupling paths.
insights.locator: In practice, interface conductors are often fractured

insights.claim: The fix for dropped cross-die coupling is to add ports on selected internal or unnamed nets during standalone die extraction and pass them to the interface preparation step, so coupling capacitors land on legal nodes; Siemens says its Calibre 3D IC extraction flow introduces these points automatically.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Automated port insertion is a differentiating feature claim in 3D IC extraction.
insights.locator: The remedy is to create connection points ahead of time.

insights.claim: A single lumped connection point per net hides where coupling occurs along long conductors running beside a 3D IC bonding interface; this may be acceptable for some digital timing checks but matters for high-frequency links, so additional ports with controllable spacing are needed.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: High-speed die-to-die links in stacked designs need higher-fidelity extraction, raising EDA tool value per design.
insights.locator: Assumption 4: One connection point per net is good enough

insights.claim: Required parasitic model accuracy depends on the analysis: compact SPEF-style parasitics may suffice for timing closure, while signal-integrity work on high-frequency 3D IC links may need RCLK, broadband or S-parameter-oriented models.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Signal-integrity modeling demand grows with high-bandwidth stacked die links.

insights.claim: All four planar-era extraction assumptions break in 3D ICs for the same reason: much of a stacked design's electrical behavior, including cross-die coupling, appears only after the dies are assembled.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: The structural shift to 3D integration expands system-level verification scope.
insights.quote: much of a stacked design’s electrical behavior, including cross-die coupling, appears only after the dies are assembled.
